$comment: Values emitted from docs/design/design-system.manifest.json that no component reads. `scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs` fails on any emitted name that is neither read nor listed here, AND on any name listed here that a component does read — both directions, because a dead exemption is how a live one gets waved through later. Every entry carries a `why` and a `cites`, and the whole list PRINTS ON EVERY RUN rather than only on a failure: an exemption nobody reads is an exemption nobody weighs. Same shape as retired-surface.json. See F-092 and .harness/plans/F-092-a-token-that-reaches-no-pixel.md.
$groupComment: `group` is required because `xs` is a radius step AND a type step, and they are not the same decision. One of them is read by 22 `size="xs"` literals; the other is read by nothing.
$readingComment: This file is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT. If it grows without anyone reading it, the citations are what makes that visible — an entry nobody can justify shows up as an entry with a weak one.

unreached.why: The web target. apps/mobile is the only surface (ADR-0051), so nothing in the reader zone imports these — their only reader is emit.test.ts, which is precisely the case this check reports. They are emitted anyway because four targets from one manifest is what stops web and mobile drifting the day a web surface exists (ADR-0020). Deleting them would remove the guarantee, not the dead code.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0051 — the web target exists so four targets cannot drift

unreached.why: Emitted to CONSTRAIN, not to paint. TEXT_TOKENS is read only through its derived `TextToken` type, which is what stops `foreground.3` compiling below the large-text floor in Text.tsx. The other three are read in real code only by packages/ui/src/testing/conformance.ts, which this check deliberately does not count as a reader — that exclusion is what makes acceptance criterion 2 mean anything. A value whose job is to be checked against is a real value with no pixel, and that difference belongs here where it can be read rather than inferred.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0054 — emitted to constrain the type, never to paint

unreached.why: Nothing in the product animates. There is no Animated, no withTiming and no transition anywhere in the reader zone — the durations and easings exist so that when something does move, the values are already decided rather than invented at the call site. The rule they belong to (motion may not animate a colour) is enforced from the manifest side by verify-motion.mjs, so it is guarded whether or not this binding is imported.

THE TRANSLUCENT DECORATIVE HAIRLINE, still painted by nothing. Every component that draws a line reaches for `border.strong` instead — the boundary of an OUTLINED control, where WCAG 1.4.11 applies directly and 3:1 is not optional. F-143 was the previous owner and did not close it, which is worth stating plainly rather than quietly re-assigning: the popover panel it added is an outlined surface and took `border.strong` like everything before it. A DECORATIVE hairline is a different thing — a rule between rows that separates without bounding, and this product has had no row list to put one between. The form controls (F-156) bring the first: a list group whose items need dividing but not enclosing. The four `.on.*` forms are permanent whatever happens to `border` itself — they are the pre-composited values the contrast gate measured, never something a component reads.

THE FOUR PRE-COMPOSITED FORMS, and what is left of an entry that also held `backdrop` itself. F-143 painted the scrim: `Popover.Overlay` takes `backdrop`, which is the first time anything in this product dimmed the page behind something — the old reason read "there is no dialog, bottom sheet or modal anywhere in the app yet", and now there is. THESE FOUR ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND RATHER THAN IN SCHEDULE, which is why they take `closedBy: null`. `backdrop.on.background` and its siblings are the values the CONTRAST GATE composited so it could measure a translucent token against each ground it may sit on — an rgba() has no contrast ratio until something is behind it. A component never reads one: it reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite. No surface will ever paint them, so no feature can close this.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0044 — the .on.* forms are what the contrast gate measured, not what a component reads: a component reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite it. No surface will ever paint them.

unreached.why: There is no chart in the product. The five-step near-achromatic ramp exists because a data series must be distinguishable without hue (golden rule 13), and deciding that under deadline is how a rainbow palette gets shipped. Wardrobe coverage and gap analysis (F-048) is the first surface that plots anything; the professional dE tables (F-055) are the second.

The token that exists to be restricted, and nothing paints it. Its usage is `largeText` — it fails AA against every surface below the WCAG large-text floor — so Text's `ColorFor<S>` type admits it only at a display or title size. The type permits it; no caller asks for it, and the one place a reader might expect it (the Home micro-label) carries a comment saying that label uses `foreground.2` and NOT this. Found only when this check stopped counting comments as reads: every mention of it in the reader zone is prose about why it is dangerous.

TWO STEPS OF A SCALE THAT IS USED. `sm`, `md`, `pill` and `swatch` are read, and F-143 added `lg` for the popover panel — the first raised surface in this product with a corner, which is why the step had found no home before. `xs` and `xl` have still found none. That is the ordinary state of a scale: some steps have not met their surface yet. It is a different thing from a scale that reaches NOTHING while hand-written values contradict it, which is what `nativeSpacing` was until F-095 — and the distinction is what decides whether an entry here is a note or a defect. The form controls (F-156) are where a smaller and a larger radius arrive.

THE TOP TWO STEPS OF THE EDITORIAL SCALE — 56 and 96 — and what is left of an entry that covered four. F-140 reached `xl2` (28) and `xl3` (40): they are `Screen`’s page inset and its rhythm between blocks, so every screen in the product now spends them and the two declarations went. THESE TWO ARE DIFFERENT, and it is worth being exact about why rather than carrying the old sentence forward. 56 and 96 are hero rhythm — the space around a single large thing, which needs a surface built around one. Every screen today is a scrolling list or a form. The first that spends one is the Atlas at photograph scale (F-147), which is also where `display.1` goes, and the two are the same design decision seen from the type side and the space side. Reaching them in F-140 would have meant painting a number to satisfy a check, which ADR-0080 names in its own honest-limit section as the failure this field exists to prevent.

THE 72px STEP. `display.2` (34px) was the other half of this entry until F-140, and it is now read by every screen in the product: `Screen` renders its title at that step, which is what closed the gap between a manifest specifying 72-to-10 and an application rendering 22-to-10. `display.1` is deliberately NOT reached by that change. It is a hero size — one element, alone, carrying a page — and a screen title is not that. Putting 72px on seventeen screen titles would have reached the token and produced a worse product, which is exactly the move ADR-0080 warns about: reach is a floor, not a design review. Its surface is Home (F-146), where the wordmark and the product name lead, and it is declared here rather than painted somewhere to make a gate quiet.

TWO OF THREE, as of F-097. `warn` is read by the Lens, which shows a capture instruction as a status rather than as prose so it carries an icon as well as its words — colour is never the only channel, and neither is a paragraph of grey text nobody scans. `ok` and `bad` are still requested by no caller: `Status` is built, conforms, and reaches gate 8 through the conformance registry, which ADR-0054 allows as a root, so nothing else reports them. The first surface that shows one is outfit scoring and explainability (F-031). This entry exists so that a status channel nobody uses stays a written-down fact rather than an assumption that it is used somewhere — and F-097 is what turned one third of it from an assumption into a reader.
